articles.title: Paraguay: President Santiago Pena under house arrest over bank crisis
Ousted Paraguay president under house arrest after banking crisis leaves 60% of country unable to access accounts

events.summary: Paraguay's Senate ousted President Santiago Peña and placed him under house arrest over the failure of a major bank linked to his administration. The banking crisis has frozen accounts for 60% of the country, trapping public pension and healthcare funds.
events.why: The unprecedented crisis paralyzes essential public services and deprives a majority of the population of their financial assets.

articles.title: Iran war: Gulf tanker attacked, 1 seaferer killed

events.summary: Iran is intensifying attacks on commercial shipping in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, leaving one seafarer dead after a Greek-owned tanker was struck. Iran also reported that two other vessels were set on fire.
events.why: Attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz threaten a critical global energy chokepoint and risk wide-scale international military escalation.

articles.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
Paraguay’s president quits after millions of people’s savings frozen in bank crisis

events.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned after a bank collapse triggered an impeachment vote in the lower house of congress. Millions of citizens' savings were left frozen due to the banking crisis.
events.why: The collapse of a major financial institution has triggered the fall of a national government and disrupted the financial security of millions.

articles.title: Why is Paraguay facing a banking and political crisis?
Ueno Bank scandal plunges Paraguay into political crisis

events.summary: The collapse of Ueno Bank has triggered a major political and banking crisis in Paraguay. The failure has raised broader concerns regarding state influence and institutional accountability.
events.why: It threatens systemic stability in Paraguay's banking system and raises serious integrity questions regarding state oversight.

articles.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
Stephen Miller named by Trump as new White House chief of staff
Stephen Miller, architect of Trump’s immigration crackdown, to become White House chief of staff

events.summary: Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. The appointment comes amid post-election staff reshuffling.
events.why: The White House chief of staff controls executive operations and policy implementation for the entire United States administration.

articles.title: Yemen’s president sacks ministers and officers in attempt to turn tide of war

events.summary: Yemen's UN-recognized government has dismissed ministers and military officers following territorial losses to the Houthis and growing pressure from southern Yemenis. The reshuffle is intended to regain lost territory and break the siege of Taiz.
events.why: A leadership shake-up in Yemen's internationally recognized government directly impacts the balance of power and civilian conditions in the civil war.

articles.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
EU prosecutor office investigates fatal train crash in Spain

events.summary: European prosecutors have opened an investigation into the use of EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish rail line where a train crash killed 69 people. Spanish rail authorities are facing fraud scrutiny as part of the probe.
events.why: The probe targets potential corruption and misuse of public safety funds linked directly to a mass-casualty rail disaster.

articles.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election

events.summary: An inconclusive Israeli election has provided the center-right opposition an opportunity to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu. Success will rely on securing the backing of Arab-led political parties.
events.why: The outcome determines the governance of Israel and could significantly alter regional diplomacy and conflict dynamics.

articles.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values

events.summary: AI stocks have rebounded after trillions of dollars were wiped from their market values in earlier sell-offs. The previous declines were driven in part by investor fears that a Democratic election victory would slow artificial intelligence development.
events.why: Large-scale fluctuations in AI valuations influence trillions in global capital allocation and tech sector investment.
